basics.name: Dr Alan Ruddock
basics.label: Associate Professor of Sport Physiology and Performance
basics.summary: Associate Professor of Sport Physiology and Performance at Sheffield Hallam University and Co-Founder of Boxing Science. CASES Fellow, Chartered Scientist, and Senior Fellow of the HEA. 38 journal publications (Google Scholar h-index 27) spanning exercise physiology, high-intensity interval training, thermoregulation, and combat sports science. Provided scientific support for 15 world title fights and multiple Commonwealth, European and British contests. Recipient of the CASES Applied Practitioner Award 2021.

projects.name: Recovery in Elite Professional Football
projects.description: Doctoral programme embedded in a Premier League club, evaluating recovery interventions.
highlights: Problem: recovery methods widely used, thinly evidenced, and expensive.
Measured: recovery interventions against performance and wellness outcomes in a Premier League environment.
Outcome: a GBP 40,000 funded doctoral programme embedded in the club.

projects.name: Hydration and Fluid Balance in Elite Squash
projects.description: Hydration status and fluid losses across a national squash squad.
highlights: Problem: fluid and sodium losses were undocumented in squash.
Measured: fluid balance, sodium losses and training-day hydration practice.
Outcome: published individualised hydration guidance, and a systematic review of the physiological and nutritional demands of the sport.

projects.name: Operational Body Armour in Specialist Police Officers
projects.description: Physiological demands and lived experience of operational body armour use.
highlights: Problem: the physiological demands and lived experience of wearing body armour on operations were not documented.
Approach: lead author of the 2020 exploratory report on heat strain under body armour, weighing cooling options against practical limits; co-author of the follow-on study of 147 officers.
Outcome: built the force's understanding of what operational body armour asks of the people wearing it.

projects.name: Heat Acclimation Before the 2014 FIFA World Cup
projects.description: Mixed-methods heat acclimation for a professional soccer match official before the Brazil tournament.
highlights: Problem: a northern European match official heading for the heat and humidity of Brazil, with no environmental chamber.
Measured: tympanic and mean body temperature, plasma volume, sweat rate, high-intensity running performance and thermal comfort.

Outcome: 13 sessions over 18 days combining isothermic running and hot water immersion. Plasma volume +7.1%, sweat rate +0.9 L/h, exercising temperature -0.6C, high-intensity running +29%. Published as a case report in SpringerPlus.
